'''Peter H. Smith''' is a professor emeritus (he retired in 2013) at the [[Lunar and Planetary Laboratory]] of the [[University of Arizona]], where he holds the inaugural [[Burr-Brown|Thomas R. Brown]] Distinguished Chair in Integrative Science.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://uanews.org/node/19742|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081203162358/http://uanews.org/node/19742|url-status=usurped|archive-date=December 3, 2008|publisher=[[University of Arizona]]|title=Peter Smith Named Thomas R. Brown Distinguished Chair in Integrative Science|author=University Communications ([[University of Arizona]])|date=2008-05-15}}</ref>  He is also the [[principal investigator]] for the $420 million robotic explorer [[Phoenix (spacecraft)|Phoenix]] which landed at the north pole of the planet [[Mars]] on May 25, 2008. Peter H. Smith's papers are held at the University of Arizona Special Collections Library.<ref>{{cite web |title=Peter Hollingsworth Smith papers finding aid |url=http://www.azarchivesonline.org/xtf/view?docId=ead/uoa/UAMS605.xml |access-date=12 June 2020}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Peter H. Smith was born December 2, 1947, in New York and was raised in Tucson, Arizona. Smith's father was Hugh H. Smith, a virologist who was part of the team at the Rockefeller Foundation who developed a vaccine for yellow fever in 1930's.  After his retirement from the Rockefeller Foundation, Hugh H. Smith worked at the University of Arizona and founded the Tucson Society of Tropical Medicine.<ref>{{Cite news|url = https://www.nytimes.com/1995/12/22/us/hugh-h-smith-is-dead-at-93-helped-to-banish-yellow-fever.html|title = The New York Times|date = December 22, 1995|access-date = April 10, 2015| last1=Saxon | first1=Wolfgang }}</ref> Smith's mother was an opera singer.

Smith went to Tucson High School and received his [[bachelor's degree]] in physics in 1969 from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] and his [[master's degree]]  from the  [[University of Arizona]] Optical Sciences Center in 1977.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://phoenix.lpl.arizona.edu/smithPeter.php|title=Peter Smith|publisher=[[University of Arizona]] Lunar and Planetary Laboratory|access-date=2008-05-10|archive-date=2018-09-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180905190759/http://phoenix.lpl.arizona.edu/smithPeter.php|url-status=dead}}</ref>  In 2009 he received a PhD in Optical Science from the University of Arizona.  Since 1978, he has worked at the University of Arizona Lunar and Planetary Laboratory, initially as a Research Assistant up the ladder to full professor with tenure.

== Space exploration missions ==
Smith  worked on the [[Pioneer Venus]] mission of 1978 and the [[Pioneer 11|Pioneer Saturn]] mission of 1979,  mapped the surface of [[Saturn]]'s largest moon [[Titan (moon)|Titan]] using the [[Hubble Space Telescope]] in 1994, and became Project Manager for a descent camera on the [[Huygens probe]] that landed on Titan in 2005.

Smith  designed the cameras for  [[Sojourner (rover)|Sojourner Rover]] of the [[Mars Pathfinder]] mission, the ill-fated [[Mars Polar Lander]], and the subsequently cancelled [[Mars Surveyor 2001 Lander|Mars Surveyor Lander]].  He helped to build the microscope for the ill-fated [[Beagle 2]], and managed the  building of the 2005 [[Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter]] [[HiRISE]] camera.  He serves on the science team for the [[Mars Exploration Rovers]] which landed in January 2004.

Smith's proposal for the [[Phoenix (spacecraft)|Phoenix]] Mars Lander project was selected in 2003 as the first [[Mars Scout Program|Scout mission to Mars]]. He was responsible for all aspects of the $420 million mission.

At present, Smith is a co-investigator for the NASA New Frontiers OSIRIS-REx Mission.

== Awards ==
Smith has received many awards in his career including the NASA Exceptional Scientific Achievement Medal in 2010.<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://www.mars-one.com/about-mars-one/advisers/peter-smith-usa|title = Peter Smith (USA)|access-date = April 10, 2015|website = Mars One}}</ref>
